expectations.criterion: [MANDATORY] uses the originating FlutterView for explicit announcements instead of the deprecated implicit-view announce API
expectations.evidence: The explicit path calls `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement(View.of(context), ...)` with the comment 'the originating window, not an implicit view'. It also says to 'delete the `announce` fallback entirely' and not to fall back to `announce` when support is false.

expectations.criterion: checks announcement support and keeps direction and message localization consistent with the originating UI
expectations.evidence: The code guards with `if (!MediaQuery.supportsAnnounceOf(context)) return;` and passes `Directionality.of(context)`. It says to take 'the view, the text direction, and the localized message from the same window's `BuildContext`' and to avoid a global navigator key, root context, or global locale.

expectations.criterion: [MANDATORY] prefers semantic state updates for ordinary feedback and does not claim assertiveness controls Android speech priority
expectations.evidence: The recommended fix for the save confirmation is visible text in a `Semantics(liveRegion: true)` node, which the response calls ordinary feedback. Explicit announcements are reserved for changes with no visible semantic node. The assertiveness argument is annotated '// currently affects web only', so it makes no claim about Android priority.

expectations.criterion: verifies the originating window and avoids duplicate feedback across semantic and explicit announcement paths
expectations.evidence: The 'No duplicate feedback' section requires one mechanism per change and says not to call `sendAnnouncement` alongside the live region or pick a different mechanism per platform. Manual desktop verification opens two windows with different locales and confirms each window speaks its own localized message once with no assertion. Android and web checks also confirm a single utterance.

judgment.summary: All four criteria are met, including both mandatory ones. The response prefers a live-region semantic update for the save confirmation and keeps an explicit announcement only for changes with no visible node. That explicit path uses `View.of(context)` with `sendAnnouncement`, checks `supportsAnnounceOf`, and takes text direction and localization from the window's own context. It says assertiveness currently affects web only, enforces a single feedback path to avoid duplicates, and includes manual verification across two windows. Minor weaknesses: the widget test does not check view identity, and the web verification guidance is vague.
